P01-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: A cut at 3:13/3:14 is the live rival, weighed here face by face and not taken. Its near face, 3:14, carries two candidate drivers at once: the transport clause וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי (oshb:Ezek.3.14), which places 3:14, like the onset verse 3:12, among the transport verses the book counts (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), and the hand-of-YHWH construct, which could be read as a fresh vision onset. Its far face, 3:13, is the sound of the creatures' wings and wheels, with no close-role formula and no parashah mark. Because a transport verb licenses a seam, the rival is not dismissed; it is held on two stated grounds. A row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and this cut would leave 3:12-13 and 3:14-15 as rows of two verses each, neither of them such a unit. And no scene change accompanies it: the same journey that begins at 3:12 continues without interruption through 3:15, so treating every occurrence of the construct as onset-grade would misclassify transit texture as a hard seam.

P10-004.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut at 40:23/40:24, weighed here face by face. Its near face, 40:24, opens the outer south gate on a transport verb (oshb:Ezek.40.24) and is a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), a licensed driver inside the vision; its far face, 40:23, ends the outer north gate on the hundred cubits measured from gate to gate (oshb:Ezek.40.23), with no formula and no mark. The cut leaves 40:20-23 and 40:24-27 at four verses each, so neither side falls under three verses and no length ground holds against it. The row holds on a stated ground: the outer court's north and south gates stand together as one measured block, and the verb at 40:24 only turns the tour toward another compass point inside the same outer court, whereas this row's own edges are larger turns in the survey, the whole-court measure closing at 40:19 behind it and the court-change transport at 40:28 ahead of it. A longer alternative, the single Ezek.40.20-Ezek.40.37 gate-circuit row (bound by the internal cross-reference 'according to these measurements'), was weighed and rejected as well: that refrain recurs at 40:24, 40:28, 40:29, 40:32, 40:33 and 40:35 (sweep: 6 verses across chapter 40), including once inside this row's own south gate at 40:24, so the refrain's distribution alone does not divide the six gates into two groups; the north gate alone is keyed to the first gate's own dimensions, standing only at 40:21 (sweep: 1 verse). The court-change transport verb at 40:28 -- a location change, unlike the compass-only transport at 40:24 -- is the stronger, byte-supported seam.

P10-012.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1, a verse of the counted transport class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens with וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר (oshb:Ezek.43.1) 'he led me to the gate', beginning the named hard seam behind the closed measuring circuit, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) and the prostration “and I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.43.3), one of five verses where the WEB reads “I fell on my face” (sweep: 5 verses). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.43.9) “Then I will dwell among them forever” (web:Ezek.43.9) immediately before the samekh (oshb:Ezek.43.9, single-witness) -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark since the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch. This is the only row here whose close carries genuine parashah corroboration, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so.

P11-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.1, a counted member of the transport class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens with a returning-transport verb that reopens the vision frame after the utterance close and double samekh at Ezek.43.27. The prophet is shown the shut east gate and told its meaning (44.2), with the prince's privilege attached (44.3); 44.4 carries a further transport verb (a fresh entry by the north gate) and closes with the prostration formula “I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.44.4), matching the vision's own inclusio elsewhere (1.28, 3.23, 11.13, 43.3). Close: the prostration at 44.4 is weighed against the immediately following verse, Ezek.44.5, which opens with a fresh son-of-man address and a directive to mark, see and hear the house's ordinances -- a class shift from vision narrative to statute. Both sides of the seam are text-signalled: the vision's own close-device on one side, a fresh address opening a distinct instructional mode on the other.
P11-001.device_notes: MT 44.3 carries an OSHB 'anomalous form' editorial note and a second editors' note recording a ketiv/qere decision relative to BHS (single-witness apparatus), both disclosed and not argued as boundary evidence. Parashah marks are disclosed in three directions, MEASURED in this witness, which records a mark ON the verse it FOLLOWS. Onset seam: corroboration IS present -- two consecutive samekh marks follow Ezek.43.27, the verse immediately before this row's first verse, and this row's own rationale argues from them. Interior, Ezek.44.1-Ezek.44.3: no mark. Close seam: no mark follows Ezek.44.4; the next mark in the book is the pe following Ezek.44.14. So the span does carry parashah corroboration, at its onset seam though not in its interior or at its close seam; each mark is single-witness and corroborates only, never deciding a seam alone. Held at medium_low, weighing the alternative close at 44.3 (the shut gate alone) against the transport-and-prostration close at 44.4.
